exposure: mode of delivery (vacuum extraction, spontaneous vaginal delivery)
phases of labor (latent, active, full dilation)
time points after delivery (2 minutes, 2 hours, 24 hours)
cohort: 167 women with low-risk, singleton, term deliveries at a tertiary academic center.
finding: Salivary cortisol concentrations increased gradually from the latent phase, peaking immediately postpartum, and then decreasing to non-gravid levels within 24 hours, while psychological stress levels peaked during latent and full dilation phases and decreased immediately postpartum.
mod_finding: Women with epidural anesthesia had lower cortisol concentrations at complete dilation and 2 hours postpartum, and cord cortisol was higher among women delivered by vacuum extraction compared with spontaneous vaginal delivery.
